fact: The Sun's nearest bright neighbour — a golden twin of the Sun anchoring the front foot of the Centaur.
bio: Rigil Kentaurus (Alpha Centauri A) is the brightest member of the closest stellar system to the Sun, just 4.3 light-years away. A near-twin of the Sun in colour and mass, it forms a bright binary with the cooler Alpha Centauri B, while the faint red dwarf Proxima Centauri orbits far out as the actual nearest star.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'foot of the Centaur'. Together with nearby Hadar it forms the 'Pointers' that guide southern observers to the Southern Cross, and as the closest Sun-like star it is a perennial target of interstellar-travel studies and fiction.
